newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures cut losses late, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures cut losses late, end lower.

text.p: Dec 17 - U.S. debt futures cut losses late, still ended lower. March T-bonds moved upward in thin trade on shortcovering as traders digested steady Fed policy, 0.6-pct rise in weekly Redbook retail sales. They had conflicting evaluations of Tuesday's technical behavior. Some said ability to close above 112-08/32 mitigated bearishness from morning's breakdown. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
"Everybody expected the Fed to do nothing, but you never know," said one Eurodollar floor broker. "It was just a bounce off the fact that the Fed did nothing."
The market got its next blip higher as news circulated that Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index rose 0.6 percent in the first two weeks December versus November.
Some traders had looked for a higher reading in the index.
Futures firmed further at the close, but action was light.
"It was so thin. You had a little bit of covering going off the lack of Fed action and the fact that Redbook wasn't as strong as some expected," said a T-bond futures floor broker.
Technically, brokers voiced slightly differing evaluations of Tuesday's performance by March T-bond futures.
The contract, pressured by strong November and upwardly revised October and September U.S. housing data Tuesday morning, punched below key support at 112-08/32 and at 112-00.
But it clawed back and closed above those areas, price behavior that some technicians said mitigated the bearishness of the morning's breakdown.
"Not overwhelmingly bad...not great," concluded the T-bond broker of the day's price action. "It would have been better to have held that 08 (112-08/32), but we settled above it."
"I think it's very devastating," said another floor broker of the breach of 112-00. "I look to see 110-12/32 to 14/32."

Futures fell early when November housing starts rose 9.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted rate of 1.514 million units, the strongest rise in 16 months. It outstripped forecasts a 1.390-million-unit rate. November permits rose 3.9 percent to 1.415 million units.

March T-bonds ended down 7/32 at 112-17/32, T-notes fell 8/32 to 109-08/32, munis lost 5/32 to 115-04/32, Eurodollars eased two bps to 94.43, and T-bills fell four bps to 94.96. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
